title: Fractalizing spacetime: Floquet codes with fractonic excitations that are immobile in space and time
abstract: We generalize fractalization, a procedure for the construction of fracton models, from space to spacetime. We apply spacetime fractalization to construct fracton floquet codes with syndrome excitations that have limited mobility in space and time. This extends the notion of fracton order to intrinsically dynamical quantum phases of matter that are inequivalent to static fracton phases. We find spacetime type-II fracton floquet codes which have no topological excitations that are mobile in space or time. These codes exhibit an extreme form of quantum discrete time crystal order with response periods that scale exponentially in their linear system sizes. In this context, the no-strings rule that characterizes type-II fractons leads to a superlinear scaling of the floquet code fault-distance with time, potentially lowering the time overhead required for quantum error correction.
summary: This paper introduces spacetime fractalization to build advanced quantum error-correcting codes known as fracton Floquet codes. By embedding fractal symmetries in both space and time, the resulting codes host excitations immobile in both dimensions. This leads to highly robust quantum memories with potentially lower time overhead for fault tolerance.
main_problem: The paper generalizes the concept of 'fractalization' from spatial dimensions to spacetime to construct novel, fault-tolerant quantum memories.
main_result: They construct an intrinsically spacetime type-II fracton Floquet code exhibiting extreme discrete time crystal order and superlinear fault-distance scaling with time.
method: The methodology involves applying fractalization techniques, originally used for constructing fracton models, to the time dimension of quantum error-correcting codes using concepts from Measurement Based Quantum Computing.
model_or_system: The focus is on constructing fracton Floquet codes based on fractal symmetries in both space and time, extending Type-II fracton order to dynamical quantum phases. The models are related to fractalized cluster states (e.g., 3D Raussendorf cluster state).
key_observables: Immobility of syndrome excitations in space and time; superlinear scaling of the Floquet code fault-distance with time; response periods scaling exponentially with system size.
important_parameters: The fractalization procedure uses linear cellular automaton (LCA) rules, such as the Sierpinski rule, applied across stacked code blocks.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on generalizing LCA dynamics to the quantum domain and assumes the applicability of the no-strings rule in the time-fractalized setting.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the discrete fractal patterns generated by the Sierpinski LCA rule and show the evolution of excitations in both time-fractalized and full spacetime type-II Floquet codes over several time steps.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first defining the spatial fractalization, then extending this concept to the time dimension using LCA rules and adaptive quantum circuits, culminating in the construction and analysis of the full spacetime type-II fracton Floquet code.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses fault-tolerance in quantum computation by proposing novel topological phases whose inherent symmetries (fracton order) lead to enhanced error correction capabilities in the time domain.
